coaching.subject: the cross-interface verification test plan

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: verify command `grep error_envelope src/rebar/*mcp*.py` greps the unanchored word 'error_envelope' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_error_envelope'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"error_envelope":')
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact resolution_class -> vocabulary-code mapping for _mcp_llm.py (or confirm all LLMError values map to the single llm_unavailable code, with resolution_class retained as the branching field).
evidence: '_mcp_llm.py:31 sets error to a vocabulary code (e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class)'
KNOWN_ERROR_CODES contains only 'llm_unavailable' for the LLM surface
findings.finding: The LLM error-code mapping is specified only by example ('e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class'), but KNOWN_ERROR_CODES lists only the single LLM code llm_unavailable. If resolution_class carries multiple values, the plan does not state how each maps to a vocabulary code, leaving the executor to invent the mapping.
scenarios: LLMError with a resolution_class value other than the one implying llm_unavailable — executor must choose an undefined code, or all LLM failures collapse to llm_unavailable losing the resolution_class distinction the plan says to preserve
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that all LLMError instances map to error=llm_unavailable while resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic are kept as additional fields for finer branching; if finer codes are wanted, add them to KNOWN_ERROR_CODES and list the mapping.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the guard's catch-list with the command_failed fallback: either have the guard catch Exception broadly (mapping unclassified to command_failed) or add an AC/step explicitly scoping AC6 to rebar-originated exceptions only.
evidence: guard 'catches RebarError (and subclasses ...), ConcurrencyMismatch, CommandError, and LLMError'
AC6: 'Every MCP error — exception-raised OR returned — carries an error code drawn from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES'
findings.finding: AC6 requires that EVERY MCP error carries an error code from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES, and error_code_for has a command_failed fallback for 'any unclassified failure', but the tool guard is described as catching only RebarError (and subclasses), ConcurrencyMismatch, CommandError, and LLMError. An unexpected non-rebar exception (e.g. KeyError/ValueError/TypeError in a tool body) would not be caught by the guard, would never reach the command_failed fallback, and would propagate as raw prose ToolError — leaving an MCP error with no envelope code.
findings.location: Design step 3(a) tool guard / AC 'Every MCP error ... carries an error code'
scenarios: A tool body raises an unanticipated Python exception (bug, unexpected input) — the agent receives unstructured prose, contradicting AC6's 'every MCP error' guarantee
findings.suggested_fix: Have the tool guard catch a broad base (e.g. except Exception) and route through error_code_for, so unclassified exceptions become command_failed envelopes; add a test that an arbitrary non-rebar exception yields error=command_failed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives explain_criterion and the LLM tool to their returned soft-error shapes and asserts BOTH the vocabulary code (criterion_unknown_id / _registry_malformed / _missing_file, llm_unavailable) AND preservation of kind / resolution_class / retryable / diagnostic.
evidence: Design 3(b): explain_criterion 'maps exc.kind ... to distinct codes ... while KEEPING a kind field'; _mcp_llm.py:31 'sets error to a vocabulary code ... while KEEPING resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic'
AC6: 'Every MCP error — exception-raised OR returned ... carries an error code ... the existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic) are PRESERVED, not dropped'

Test plan per-code pinning lists only 'ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, plus command_failed fallback' — no test named for the returned-shape codes or the field-preservation assertion
findings.finding: The two RETURN-shaped soft-error migrations (explain_criterion's kind→code mapping in _mcp_reads.py:77 and _mcp_llm.py:31's vocabulary code) are asserted by AC6 to gain a vocabulary code WHILE PRESERVING kind / resolution_class / retryable / diagnostic, but the Test plan lists no test that exercises these returned shapes end-to-end. Per-code pinning names only exception-raised codes (ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, command_failed); the criterion_unknown_id / criterion_registry_malformed / criterion_missing_file / llm_unavailable return-shape codes and their preserved auxiliary fields are untested.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the AC2 vocabulary-closure assertion to also cover the inline 'error' codes emitted by the two RETURN-shaped soft-error sites (_mcp_reads.py explain_criterion, _mcp_llm.py), not only literals passed to error_envelope(...), so no MCP-emitted code can escape KNOWN_ERROR_CODES.
evidence: Plan: 'every literal code passed to error_envelope(...) across src/rebar/ is a member of KNOWN_ERROR_CODES'
Design 3(b): the two return-shaped sites 'set error to a vocabulary code' but the plan (and _mcp_reads.py:84 / _mcp_llm.py:31) build dicts inline, not via error_envelope(...)
AC2/AC6: 'a code cannot exist on one interface only' / 'MCP can only emit members'
findings.finding: The AC2 vocabulary-closure mechanism is scoped to 'every literal code passed to error_envelope(...)', but the two RETURN-shaped soft-error sites build {'error': code} dicts inline WITHOUT calling error_envelope(...), so their codes (criterion_unknown_id/criterion_registry_malformed/criterion_missing_file, llm_unavailable) are not covered by the closure check even though AC6 requires 'MCP can only emit members'.
findings.location: Test plan > Vocabulary closure (AC2); Design item 3(b)
scenarios: A future edit sets a mistyped inline 'error' code in explain_criterion or the LLM soft-error path; the error_envelope(...)-scoped closure test passes, so a non-vocabulary code ships over MCP undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert closure over the union of (codes passed to error_envelope(...)) and (the kind_to_code values in _mcp_reads.py plus the _mcp_llm.py 'error' code), or route the two inline sites through a shared helper that validates against KNOWN_ERROR_CODES.

findings.finding: The plan adds vocabulary codes to the two RETURN-shaped soft-error paths (_mcp_reads.py:77 explain_criterion mapping exc.kind to criterion_unknown_id/criterion_registry_malformed/criterion_missing_file, and _mcp_llm.py:31 setting error to llm_unavailable) but the test plan's per-code pinning enumerates only ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, and command_failed — none of these newly-migrated return-shaped codes are named in any test, so the migration of the two ad-hoc shapes could ship without a test proving each emits its vocabulary code while preserving kind/resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic.
findings.location: Test plan (held-out oracle); AC6 (Every MCP error... carries an error code... fields PRESERVED)
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the per-code pinning and preservation tests to cover the return-shaped codes: for each kind assert both the vocabulary error code (a KNOWN_ERROR_CODES member) and the retained companion field(s).

findings.finding: Step 3(b) says the _mcp_llm.py error code is 'e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class', implying a mapping from resolution_class values to codes, but KNOWN_ERROR_CODES lists only the single LLM code llm_unavailable — leaving unstated whether all resolution_class values collapse to llm_unavailable or whether additional per-class codes are intended.
findings.suggested_fix: State that all LLM resolution_class values map to the single vocabulary code llm_unavailable (the only LLM member of KNOWN_ERROR_CODES), with resolution_class preserved as an additional discriminating field.

findings.finding: The _mcp_llm.py return-path design is internally inconsistent: it says the error code is 'derived from its resolution_class', but resolution_class is a closed 8-value enum (WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW, INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS, CHANGE_SETTINGS, CHANGE_INPUT, CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL, FIX_AGENT_DESIGN, NEEDS_INVESTIGATION) while KNOWN_ERROR_CODES lists only the single code llm_unavailable for this path. Either the derivation collapses all 8 classes to llm_unavailable (making 'derived from resolution_class' misleading) or it produces per-class codes absent from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES (violating the vocabulary-closure AC2 the plan asserts).
findings.location: Design section item 3(b): '_mcp_llm.py:31 sets error to a vocabulary code (e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class)'
findings.suggested_fix: Set `error` to the constant `llm_unavailable` for the LLMError return-path (matching the classifier's single LLMError->llm_unavailable mapping), and keep resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic as the preserved branch signal — drop the 'derived from resolution_class' phrasing, since the discriminator is intentionally coarse and the fine-grained signal lives in the preserved fields.
